commit.message:
Add six Cogentic research papers:

- "Unconditional Integer Factorization in Time L_N[1/3, O(1)]" (`integer_factorization/`)
- "Discrete Logarithms in Finite Fields of Fixed Characteristic in Sub-Quasi-Polynomial Time" (`discrete_logarithm/`)
- "An Exact Polynomial-Time Algorithm for 1/5-Approximate Nash Equilibria in Bimatrix Games" (`bimatrix_nash_equilibrium/`)
- "Unconditional Deterministic Subexponential Integer Factoring and Quadratic Nonresidue Construction" (`deterministic_factoring_l34/`)
- "Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for the Log-Rank Conjecture" (`logrank_conjecture/`)
- "Unconditional Edge Reconstruction of Simple Graphs of Linear Density" (`edge_reconstruction/`)

These papers were generated by the Cogentic harness. Lean 4 formalizations of all six proofs will be released in a companion submission.

+# An Exact Polynomial-Time Algorithm for $1/5$-Approximate Nash Equilibria in Bimatrix Games
+
+[This paper](paper.pdf) constructs an explicit deterministic algorithm,
+$\textsc{MaximinKiteNE}$, that, given any integers $m, n \ge 1$ and any
+two-player normal-form (bimatrix) game $G = (R, C)$ with rational payoff
+matrices $R, C \in ([0, 1] \cap \mathbb{Q})^{m \times n}$ of total binary
+encoding length $L$, runs in deterministic time $\operatorname{poly}(L)$ and
+outputs a rational mixed strategy profile $(x^{\mathrm{out}}, y^{\mathrm{out}})$
+in $(\Delta_m \cap \mathbb{Q}^m) \times (\Delta_n \cap \mathbb{Q}^n)$
+of binary encoding length $\operatorname{poly}(L)$ satisfying maximum unilateral
+regret
+
+$$f(x^{\mathrm{out}}, y^{\mathrm{out}}) \le \frac{1}{5}.$$
+
+This establishes an exact polynomial-time $r$-approximation ($\delta = 0$) at
+$r = 1/5$—improving the previous polynomial-time barrier of $1/3 + \delta$—and
+immediately yields a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS)
+at threshold $r = 1/5$ computing a rational $(1/5 + \delta)$-approximate Nash
+equilibrium for every rational $\delta > 0$ in time
+$\operatorname{poly}(L) \le \operatorname{poly}(L, 1/\delta)$. A complete,
+unconditional, Mathlib-only Lean 4 (`v4.35.0`) formalization of the entire proof
+has also been completed and will be released in a companion submission.
+
+This paper and its Lean 4 formalization were entirely obtained by Cogentic
+(arXiv preprint [arXiv:2609.40324](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40324)), an
+agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model.
+There was no human interaction other than the initial prompt for Cogentic to
+generate a full proof and formalization.
+The Cogentic harness was built by Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang,
+Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, and Di Wang (Google Research
+and Google DeepMind).

+# Unconditional Deterministic Subexponential Integer Factoring and Quadratic Nonresidue Construction
+
+[This paper](paper.pdf) constructs explicit,
+parameter-free deterministic algorithms for general integer factoring,
+$(p - 1)$-multiple order splitting, and computing quadratic nonresidues modulo
+odd primes:
+
+1. **General integer factoring (Theorem 1.1):** An explicit deterministic
+   algorithm `algFactor` that, given any composite integer $N \ge 4$, outputs a
+   nontrivial divisor $1 < d < N$ of $N$ in worst-case bit-operation complexity
+   $O\!\bigl(\exp(3\,(\ln N)^{3/4})\bigr) = L_N[3/4, o(1)]$, where
+   $$
+   L_x(\alpha, c) := \exp\!\bigl(c\,(\ln x)^\alpha (\ln\ln x)^{1-\alpha}\bigr).
+   $$
+2. **Order splitting and prime quadratic nonresidues (Theorem 1.2):**
+   - An explicit deterministic algorithm `algSplit` that, given any composite
+     non-perfect-power $N \ge 4$ and any even integer $\widetilde{M} \ge 2$
+     divisible by $p - 1$ for every prime factor $p \mid N$, outputs a
+     nontrivial divisor $1 < d < N$ of $N$ in worst-case bit-operation
+     complexity
+     $$
+     \exp\!\bigl(O((\ln N)^{1/2} \ln\ln N)\bigr)
+     \cdot (\ln \widetilde{M})(\ln N)^2.
+     $$
+   - An explicit deterministic algorithm `algQnr` that, given any odd prime
+     $p \ge 3$, outputs an integer $z \in \{1, \dots, p - 1\}$ with Legendre
+     symbol $\bigl(\frac{z}{p}\bigr) = -1$ in worst-case bit-operation
+     complexity $\exp\!\bigl(O((\ln p)^{1/2} \ln\ln p)\bigr) = L_p[1/2, O(1)]$.
+3. **Deterministic $(p - 1)$-exponent annihilation (Theorem 1.3):** An explicit
+   deterministic subroutine `algExp` that, given any odd composite
+   non-perfect-power integer $N \ge 9$, runs in worst-case time
+   $O\!\bigl(\exp(3\,(\ln N)^{3/4})\bigr)$ and either outputs a nontrivial
+   divisor of $N$ directly or outputs an even integer $\widetilde{M} \ge 2$
+   with $\ln \widetilde{M} \le \exp\!\bigl((\ln N)^{0.65}\bigr)$ and
+   $(p - 1) \mid \widetilde{M}$ for every prime factor $p \mid N$.
+
+A complete, unconditional, Mathlib-only Lean 4 (`v4.33.0`) formalization of the
+entire proof has also been completed and will be released in a companion
+submission.
+
+This paper and its Lean 4 formalization were entirely obtained by Cogentic
+(arXiv preprint [arXiv:2609.40324](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40324)), an
+agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model.
+There was no human interaction other than the initial prompt for Cogentic to
+generate a full proof and formalization.
+The Cogentic harness was built by Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang,
+Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, and Di Wang (Google Research
+and Google DeepMind).

+# Discrete Logarithms in Finite Fields of Fixed Characteristic in Sub-Quasi-Polynomial Time
+
+[This paper](paper.pdf) gives an unconditional classical zero-error Las Vegas
+algorithm for the Discrete Logarithm Problem in the multiplicative group
+$\mathbb{F}_{p^n}^\times$ of any finite field of small characteristic: on every
+prime $p \ge 2$, integer $n \ge 1$, degree-$n$ monic irreducible
+$f \in \mathbb{F}_p[X]$ presenting $\mathbb{F}_{p^n} = \mathbb{F}_p[X]/(f(X))$,
+and nonzero $g, h \in \mathbb{F}_{p^n}^\times$, it either returns an integer
+$x \in \{0, \dots, p^n - 2\}$ with $g^x = h$ or returns an explicit exponent
+$E \in \{1, \dots, p^n - 1\}$ certifying $h \notin \langle g \rangle$ (with
+$g^E = 1$ and $h^E \ne 1$, without factoring $p^n - 1$), in worst-case expected
+bit complexity
+
+$$
+\exp\!\left(\frac{2 + o(1)}{\ln\ln\ln n}\,(\ln n)^2\right) = (pn)^{o(\log n)}
+$$
+
+for every fixed prime $p \ge 2$ as $n \to \infty$ (and uniformly whenever
+$\ln p \le \frac{1}{4}(\ln\ln\ln n)^2$), and
+$\exp(o((\ln n)^2)) = (pn)^{o(\log n)}$ along every sequence with
+$n \to \infty$ and $(\ln p)/(\ln\ln n) \to 0$. A complete, unconditional,
+Mathlib-only Lean 4 (`v4.35.0`) formalization of the entire proof has also been
+completed and will be released in a companion submission.
+
+This paper and its Lean 4 formalization were entirely obtained by Cogentic
+(arXiv preprint [arXiv:2609.40324](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40324)), an
+agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model.
+There was no human interaction other than the initial prompt for Cogentic to

+The Cogentic harness was built by Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang,

+# Unconditional Edge Reconstruction of Simple Graphs of Linear Density
+
+[This paper](paper.pdf) resolves Harary's (1964)
+Edge Reconstruction Conjecture for all finite simple graphs of linear edge
+density above an explicit constant threshold:
+
+1. **Linear-density edge reconstruction (Theorem 1.1):** Every finite simple
+   undirected graph $G_0$ on $n_0 \ge 4$ vertices with
+   $m = |E(G_0)| \ge 1000\, n_0$ edges is edge-reconstructible (uniquely
+   determined up to isomorphism by the multiset
+   $\mathcal{D}_E(G_0) = \{\!\{[G_0 - e] : e \in E(G_0)\}\!\}$ of its
+   unlabelled single-edge-deleted subgraphs).
+2. **Minimum-degree corollary (Corollary 1.2):** Every finite simple undirected
+   graph $G_0$ with minimum degree $\delta(G_0) \ge 2000$ is
+   edge-reconstructible.
+
+Previously, the strongest unconditional density bound valid for arbitrary simple
+graphs was Müller's $m > n \log_2 n$ (1977), refining Lovász's
+$m > \frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{2}$ (1972); other unconditional results require extra
+structure, such as $m > n \log_2 \Delta(G) + O(n)$ or a bounded-degree spanning
+tree (Caro, Krasikov, and Roditty 1985). A complete, unconditional, Mathlib-only
+Lean 4 (`v4.33.0`) formalization of the entire proof has also been completed and
+will be released in a companion submission.
+
+This paper and its Lean 4 formalization were entirely obtained by Cogentic
+(arXiv preprint [arXiv:2609.40324](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40324)), an
+agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model.
+There was no human interaction other than the initial prompt for Cogentic to

+The Cogentic harness was built by Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang,

+# Unconditional Integer Factorization in Time $L_N[1/3, O(1)]$
+
+[This paper](paper.pdf) constructs an unconditional, zero-error Las Vegas
+algorithm on a single fixed uniform classical multitape Turing machine
+$\mathcal{M}$ that computes the exact complete prime factorization
+$N = \prod_{1 \le i \le k} p_i^{e_i}$ ($p_1 < \dots < p_k$ prime, $e_i \ge 1$)
+of every integer $N \ge 2$ given in standard binary representation, halting
+with probability $1$ over its read-once fair coin flips, in worst-case expected
+time $L_N[1/3, 105]$ and worst-case deterministic workspace $L_N[1/3, 40]$,
+where
+
+$$L_x(\alpha, c) := \exp\!\bigl(c\,(\ln x)^\alpha (\ln\ln x)^{1-\alpha}\bigr)$$
+
+and $T(N) \le L_N[\alpha, c]$ means
+
+$$
+\limsup_{N \to \infty}
+\frac{\ln \max(1, T(N))}{(\ln N)^\alpha (\ln\ln N)^{1-\alpha}} \le c.
+$$
+
+Every prime factor in the output is certified deterministically via
+Agrawal–Kayal–Saxena primality testing and direct multiplication against $N$,
+with effectively computable constants and no unproven number-theoretic
+hypotheses. A complete, unconditional, Mathlib-only Lean 4 (`v4.35.0`)
+formalization of the entire proof has also been completed and will be released
+in a companion submission.
+
+This paper and its Lean 4 formalization were entirely obtained by Cogentic
+(arXiv preprint [arXiv:2609.40324](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40324)), an
+agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model.
+There was no human interaction other than the initial prompt for Cogentic to
+generate a full proof and formalization.
+The Cogentic harness was built by Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang,
+Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, and Di Wang (Google Research

+# Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for the Log-Rank Conjecture
+
+[This paper](paper.pdf) proves a polynomial
+improvement over Lovett's $O(\sqrt{r} \log r)$ bound for the Lovász–Saks
+log-rank conjecture. Setting $\varepsilon := 5 \times 10^{-6}$, $C := 2^{38}$,
+and $C' := 750\,C$, every Boolean matrix $M \in \{0, 1\}^{X \times Y}$ of real
+rank $r = \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(M) \ge 1$ over finite nonempty sets
+$X, Y$ satisfies:
+
+1. There exists an $M$-monochromatic combinatorial rectangle
+   $A \times B \subseteq X \times Y$ of density
+   $$\frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|X| \cdot |Y|} \ge 2^{-C\, r^{1/2 - \varepsilon}}.$$
+2. Whenever $r \ge 2$, the monochromatic partition number $\chi(M)$ and
+   deterministic two-party communication complexity $D^{\mathrm{cc}}(M)$ satisfy
+   $$\log_2 \chi(M) \le D^{\mathrm{cc}}(M) \le C'\, r^{1/2 - \varepsilon}.$$
+
+The proof reduces monochromatic rectangle density via Gaussian hyperplane
+rounding and box-constrained biasing to refuting the existence of biased
+Kullback–Leibler-stable sign matrices $S \in \{-1, +1\}^{X \times Y}$ of rank
+at most $r + 1$ above $R_0 := \lceil e^{4 \times 10^6} \rceil$ (Theorem 3.1).
+A complete, unconditional, Mathlib-only Lean 4 (`v4.33.0`) formalization of the
+entire proof has also been completed and will be released in a companion
+submission.
+

+(arXiv preprint [arXiv:2609.40324](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40324)), an
+agentic framework for mathematical discovery, using Gemini 4 as the base model.
